audits.basis: FOLLOW-UP SPLITS THE PRIOR UNRESOLVED VERDICT INTO THREE PARTS, PRESERVING SCOPE. (1) Attribution to Lord 1960 (§10): CONTRADICTED. The complete 1960 transcription contains no occurrence of '12,323' (grep count 0, re-verified this round on the same 869,106-byte local copy); the 1960 wording is 'his dictated version runs to over 12,000 lines', so the exact numeral is not Lord's 1960 count. (2) Performance framing (§1): CONTRADICTED. Every retrieved source characterises the 12,323-line Parry 6840 text as a dictation taken down over five days ('Avdo dictated, over five days, ... 12,323 lines long'; Lord 1960: 'dictated version', 'Avdo had been singing and dictating for several weeks'), not a single sung performance; the 13,331-line Osmanbey Delibegović was likewise sung 'over several days'. (3) The numeral itself: SUPPORTED (partially) as the standard count of the 1935 dictated text, now traced past 1960 to Lord's later Lord 1991 (Epic Singers and Oral Tradition, ch. 4, pp. 57-68) via the Wikipedia citation apparatus, which quotes Lord's comparison 'Krauss's text has 2,160 lines; Avdo's in 1935 had 12,323 lines and in 1950, 8,488 lines' (footnoted to Lord 1991 pp. 60-61). This is partial support of the figure's existence and standardness, not whole-claim confirmation: the row as worded ('in one performance'; 'Lord's own count (Lord 1960)') fails on both attributions, so the verdict is contradicted.
audits.coupling_implication: The row is a language/poetry machinery claim (oral-formulaic expansion under performance pressure) coupled to a 1930s Bosnia-Herzegovina guslar era. The corrections touch figures and framing only: dictation is a distinct compositional situation from sung performance (Lord 1960 ch. 2 treats the two separately), and the exact count belongs to Lord 1991, not Lord 1960. Any downstream system rule keyed to '12,323 lines in one performance' should read 'a dictated text of 12,323 lines, taken down over five days (Parry 6840; count as given in Lord 1991)', kept distinct from sung lengths (8,488 lines for Meho in 1950; 13,331 lines for Osmanbey Delibegović across several days). Myth/era/dress content of the entry is untouched by this audit.
audits.limits: Lord 1991 itself and the 1974 Harvard UP first printing (Serbo-Croatian Heroic Songs vol. 1) were not retrievable: both archive.org scans are lending-restricted and the anonymous search-inside endpoint refuses ('Item not available'); WebSearch was quota-blocked (HTTP 403); no institutional access. The p.-level Lord 1991 anchor therefore rests on the Wikipedia citation apparatus (tertiary source), not on the book's own retrieved pages, and whether the 1974 preface also states 'Lord's own count' remains unverified. Exact-figure provenance is narrowed to Lord 1991 with high confidence but is not confirmed against primary pages.

audits.basis: BIBLIOGRAPHIC CONFLICT RESOLVED; TRUE BIBLIOGRAPHIC CORRECTION CONFIRMED. Four independent records (Crossref publisher-deposited AAAS metadata, OpenAlex, NCBI/PubMed PMID 30872490, Europe PMC) agree: Blasi, Moran, Moisik, Widmer, Dediu & Bickel (2019), 'Human sound systems are shaped by post-Neolithic changes in bite configuration', Science 363(6432): eaav3218, published 15 March 2019. The entry's L62 citation ('*Science* 363: eaav3218') is correct in journal, volume and article number (issue 6432 is additionally available); L36's '*Science* 366' matches no authoritative record consulted (Science volume 366 is a later 2019 volume of the same journal), so L36 is a genuine bibliographic error that the parent may warrant as erratum from these retrieved records. SCOPE SEPARATION: this resolves the venue metadata only. The separate diet/bite-configuration to phonetics causal argument is a content claim; its abstract was retrieved (Europe PMC core record, scratch europepmc_aav3218.json: 'labiodental sounds (such as "f" and "v") were innovated after the Neolithic. Changes in diet attributable to food-process[ing]') and shows what the argument asserts (post-Neolithic diet change driving labiodental innovation), but its truth is neither confirmed nor denied by this audit, and the published rebuttal/response debate already listed in the entry (Tarasov & Uyeda 2020; Blasi et al. 2020 response; Berthommier & Boë 2019) is untouched. The prior row's 'unresolved' therefore becomes: disagreement real (supported), correct reading identified, causal content still out of scope.
audits.coupling_implication: The paper supplies the era (post-Neolithic) x language (cross-linguistic sound-inventory statistics) coupling discussed in the entry's bite-configuration debate block. Confirming the venue does not confirm the coupling content; the causal argument must continue to be cited as contested, and any downstream use of this row must not read the bibliographic fix as evidence for the diet-to-phonetics claim. No myth/era/dress implications beyond what the entry already states.
